Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

fasttrop 0.1.0

This is the first version of the package.

Estimator

  • The package calculates the Triply Robust Panel (TROP) estimator of Athey, Imbens, Qu, and Viviano (2026).
  • The local method (method = "local") is the estimator of the paper for each treated cell. The global method (method = "global") is the block estimator of the Python package from the authors.
  • Leave-one-out cross-validation or placebo cross-validation selects the tuning parameters.
  • The unit bootstrap of Algorithm 3 gives standard errors. The default confidence interval is a normal interval. A percentile interval is also available.

Speed

  • The model fits run in C with OpenMP and with the BLAS and LAPACK libraries of R. The number of threads does not change the results.
  • On Windows, the C code tells Windows not to use power throttling on its threads while it runs. Power throttling can make a long calculation in an R session slower. To keep the usual Windows policy, use trop_control(throttle = TRUE).
  • The function trop_threads() gives at most 2 threads when R CMD check sets the environment variable _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_.

Documentation

  • The package has a website with articles in plain words: https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/.
  • The vignette “Get started with fasttrop” shows a first analysis step by step.
  • citation("fasttrop") gives the references for the paper and the package.

On this page

Developed by Alex Farach. The TROP method is from Athey, Imbens, Qu, and Viviano (2026). The authors of the method did not write this package.
